query: What signals suggest a support ticket will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: has_technical_issue
per_column.rationale: A technical vs non-technical split is a genuinely useful axis for predicting resolution time. However the values contradict the source: CS-0002 (session-drop bug) and CS-0005 (BOM export bug) are plainly technical yet labelled 0, undermining groundedness.

per_column.name: is_customer_blocked
per_column.rationale: Whether the customer is blocked is a strong signal for urgency/effort. Labels are mostly defensible (CS-0003 outage blocking a presentation = 1), though CS-0002/CS-0005 as 'blocked' is a stretch (they have workarounds), a mild overreach.

per_column.name: needs_investigation
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket requires investigation/RCA is a plausible driver of longer resolution. CS-0003 (RCA requested) correctly 1; CS-0002 (suspected SSO push needing confirmation) and CS-0005 (diagnosing BOM cause) arguably warrant investigation but are 0, a somewhat conservative but not clearly wrong read.

per_column.name: has_external_integration
per_column.rationale: External integration (SSO, Snowflake pipeline) adds coordination complexity, a reasonable signal. Values are well grounded: CS-0002 (SSO) and CS-0005 (Snowflake) correctly 1, CS-0001 billing correctly 0.

per_column.name: affects_multiple_users
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact is a solid axis for resolution effort, but grounding is weak: CS-0004 (single power-user enhancement) marked 1 with no support, while CS-0002 (single user) is 0 as expected. The high 1-rate (115) plus the CS-0004 error suggest over-assertion.

judge.rationale: All five columns give binary complexity/impact signals that are genuinely relevant to predicting longer resolution times, offering distinct axes (technical nature, blocking, investigation, integration, scope) rather than restatements—so analytical usefulness is high. Groundedness is mixed: has_external_integration and needs_investigation are well-read from the text, but has_technical_issue mislabels obvious technical bugs as non-technical, and affects_multiple_users asserts multi-user impact for a clearly single-user enhancement request, both indicating hallucinated values that a strict evaluator must penalise.
